Clinical significance vs user APS: not reported in the information source
Sample type: Patient serum previously measured with the same method ('known original value'); up to 10 patients' samples per immunoassay; 533 patients and 3128 measurements in total across all 59 assays
Study method details: Each patient's serum divided into five samples of 180 µL and spiked with 20 µL biotin solution of 100, 300, 500, 1000 or 1500 ng/ml (lyophilized biotin, Sigma-Aldrich >=99%, #B4501, Lot. SLBZ5374, in standard NaCl solution), giving biotin increases of 10, 30, 50, 100 or 150 ng/ml; assays repeated on a Cobas e801, measured values multiplied by 1.1 to compensate for dilution and related to the 'known original value' as a recovery coefficient
Additional sources of bias: Digoxin results are not reported individually in this PDF - only the pooled mean of the 18 competitive immunoassays is shown (Figure 4); the per-assay mean recovery coefficients are in Table S2, a supplement not contained in this PDF; authors state "the changes in the measured values of the competitive immunoassays and the sandwich immunoassays are not binding for the tested methods"; pre-existing serum biotin was not measured; samples were diluted and back-corrected by a factor 1.1; the standard deviation of the recovery coefficient for competitive immunoassays rises from 0.40 at 10 ng/ml to 1.02 at 150 ng/ml
Notes: Digoxin was tested (it is named in the Figure 4 caption among the competitive immunoassays) but this PDF prints NO digoxin-specific baseline, measured value, recovery coefficient, direction or percentage: "Due to this summary, the individual biotin interference of each immunoassay is not shown", and the per-assay data live in Table S2, a supplement not contained in this PDF. The pooled competitive-immunoassay result is an increase in measured values, but the authors explicitly caution that "the changes in the measured values of the competitive immunoassays and the sandwich immunoassays are not binding for the tested methods", so no direction and no magnitude can be attributed to digoxin from this source and no comparison against the user APS of 3% is possible. The pooled figure is transcribed verbatim in the Magnitude column for reference only.
